forces.title: Maturing Renewable Supply-Side Market and Shifting Growth Drivers
forces.description: McKinsey observes a structural shift where growth in power conversion technologies for supply-side renewable energy (e.g., solar PV) is slowing, with solar PV CAGR declining by 2% from 2024-2030. Concurrently, demand-side electrification (data centers, EVs) is rapidly accelerating. This indicates a maturing renewable generation sector and a new phase where integrating and efficiently utilizing generated clean power across diverse consumption points becomes the primary growth vector for power conversion technologies.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Electrolyzer Rectifier Market Growth Moderated by Project Delays
forces.description: McKinsey notes that the rapid scale-up expected for electrolyzer rectifier applications has seen expectations moderated due to project delays and cancellations. Despite a projected 26% annual growth to $0.6 billion by 2030, this slowdown relative to earlier deployment announcements acts as a headwind, impacting the pace of green hydrogen infrastructure development and associated equipment demand. Competition is intensifying for compact, high-efficiency, plug-and-play rectifiers to counter this trend.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Residential & Commercial Solar PV Inverter Market Faces Price Compression
forces.description: McKinsey forecasts a 4% annual decline in the residential and commercial solar PV power conversion equipment market to $13 billion by 2030. This contraction is driven by intense pricing pressure and market saturation in mature regions. Despite declining value pools, competition remains high, pushing players to focus on cost optimization and product differentiation through hybrid and smart-inverter capabilities, along with expanding into adjacent services like energy management and storage integration.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Utility-Scale Solar PV Inverter Market Shrinking Due to Price Competition
forces.description: McKinsey projects a 2% decline in the global utility-scale solar PV power conversion equipment market to $7.6 billion by 2030. This contraction is primarily fueled by severe price compression and escalating competition. Despite declining market size, compliance with stringent grid codes and the integration of grid-stabilizing features are becoming increasingly critical differentiators, especially following grid instability events in regions like Spain and Portugal, pushing developers to focus on technological resilience alongside cost efficiency.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Total Cost of Ownership Driving Price Pressure on Solar PV and BESS
forces.description: A McKinsey survey of solar PV and BESS customers in Europe and the US highlights Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) as the most critical purchasing criterion. This intense focus on TCO indicates significant price pressure across these markets, leading to margin compression for manufacturers and developers of solar PV and battery energy storage systems. Consequently, this pressure contributes to the projected market size contraction for solar PV power conversion equipment, pushing companies to prioritize cost optimization strategies.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Diverging Dynamics in Power Conversion Segments: Complexity vs. Commoditization
forces.description: McKinsey identifies a structural divergence in the power conversion market. High-complexity segments like data centers, HVDC, and BESS are rewarding players who deliver end-to-end solutions and software-driven capabilities such as grid-forming control. Conversely, lower-complexity segments like solar PV and space/water heat pumps are experiencing intense price compression and commoditization, shifting competition primarily to cost optimization and supply chain scale. This requires distinct strategic approaches for equipment players and investors depending on their chosen market segment.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Hybrid AC/DC Power Architecture Emerging for High-Density Applications
forces.description: BCG highlights a quiet rewiring of the world's energy system towards a hybrid AC/DC architecture. With dominant new energy sources (solar PV) and loads (batteries, EVs, data centers) being natively DC, there's an increasing mismatch with AC distribution. This structural shift will see AC remain the grid backbone while DC powers high-density, behind-the-meter applications in data centers, industrial plants, and commercial buildings. This transition, driven by efficiency and power density needs, aims to reduce conversion losses and optimize energy use, creating new opportunities for DC-native clean energy technologies.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Fragmented Standards and Workforce Gaps Hinder Hybrid AC/DC Adoption
forces.description: BCG identifies fragmented standards and a lack of DC-specific workforce expertise as real barriers to faster adoption of hybrid AC/DC power architectures. Despite technological readiness and compelling economics in high-density applications, inconsistent standards across regions increase costs and slow deployment. Furthermore, most electrical engineers and electricians lack the necessary capabilities for designing, protecting, integrating, and commissioning DC systems. Addressing these non-technological challenges through aligned standards and targeted retraining is critical to accelerating the energy transition.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: BESS Tender Pipeline Conversion to Operational Capacity is Under 1%
forces.description: EY-Parthenon highlights a critical risk in India's BESS market: despite a rapidly scaling tender pipeline of ~111 GWh, less than 1% has translated into operational capacity. Approximately 30% of tendered capacity has not progressed due to cancellations, delays, or lack of Power Sale Agreements (PSA), with 70% still in pre-commissioning stages. This significant gap between tenders and actual deployment underscores that execution across PSA closure, financing, and commissioning is the primary constraint, delaying India's BESS growth story.
forces.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

forces.title: India's BESS Supply Chain Faces Critical Upstream & Midstream Gaps
forces.description: EY-Parthenon reveals significant structural gaps in India's domestic BESS supply chain, despite rapid cell-to-pack capacity build-out. Acute gaps exist in critical minerals, battery-grade refining, cathode/anode active materials, and electrolyte salts, which account for 60-70% of battery costs. Midstream bottlenecks include separator films and manufacturing equipment. Without targeted policy interventions focusing on mineral security, processing infrastructure, technology partnerships, and duty rationalization, India risks building downstream assembly capacity while remaining import-dependent for strategically sensitive battery components, hindering long-term competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

forces.title: Declining Battery Costs and Stabilizing Li-ion Pack Prices Boost BESS Economics
forces.description: EY-Parthenon notes that battery raw material prices, particularly lithium, have corrected sharply from late 2022 peaks, leading to a ~35% decline in Li-ion pack prices that are now expected to stabilize at lower levels. This development significantly improves project economics and supports financial closure for BESS deployments in India. The current cost environment creates a crucial deployment window, enhancing tariff viability and making projects more bankable, although procurement timing, Forex exposure, and lifecycle cost assumptions remain critical for sustained viability.
forces.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

forces.title: Rebound in India's Standalone BESS Tariffs Signals Underpriced Lifecycle Costs
forces.description: EY-Parthenon observes a sharp decline in India's standalone BESS tariffs by ~85% from INR10.83 lakh/MW/month to sub-INR2 lakh levels, driven by falling battery costs and competition. However, recent trends show a rebound despite stable battery prices, suggesting that earlier bids likely underpriced crucial lifecycle costs such as financing, degradation, augmentation, and execution risks. This tariff evolution indicates a transition from initial discovery to a more bankable pricing phase, where realistic cost assumptions are critical, posing a headwind to project viability if not accurately factored.
forces.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

forces.title: India Opens Civil Nuclear Market to Private and Foreign Participation
forces.description: EY highlights the structural shift initiated by India's SHANTI Act in December 2025, opening the civil nuclear market to private and foreign participation at scale. This landmark legislation enables private entities to build, own, operate, and decommission nuclear plants, departing from a historically state-led model. While foreign participation is routed through India-incorporated JVs to retain Indian majority ownership, this framework creates a significant opportunity for global players to engage across technology, project development, financing, and lifecycle services, transforming India into a long-term ecosystem play for nuclear energy.
forces.source_title: How India’s nuclear ambition can power the next global clean energy push

forces.title: Bharat Small Reactors (BSRs) Offer Industrial Decarbonization Pathway
forces.description: EY identifies Bharat Small Reactors (BSRs), India's indigenous 220 MW SMRs, as a key upside driver for industrial decarbonization. By providing high-reliability, 24x7 firm power with zero operational emissions, BSRs are well-suited for co-located industrial demand centers such as data centers, metals & mining, and chemical manufacturing. Their LCOE of US$50–US$120/MWh compares favorably with diesel backup and avoids intermittency, creating bankable opportunities for global players in localized supply chains and technology partnerships for distributed and industrial applications.
forces.source_title: How India’s nuclear ambition can power the next global clean energy push

forces.title: India's FDI Restrictions Limit Direct Foreign Ownership in Nuclear Sector
forces.description: EY highlights that while India's civil nuclear market is open to private participation, foreign direct investment (FDI) in licensed atomic energy activities remains a prohibited sector under FEMA. Foreign-incorporated entities cannot directly obtain licenses and must participate through India-incorporated joint ventures or structured arrangements, maintaining Indian majority ownership. Although equipment manufacture and supply activities are permitted for FDI, the overarching restriction on direct ownership of nuclear assets represents a key risk and structural constraint for international players seeking deeper control and participation in India's nuclear expansion.
forces.source_title: How India’s nuclear ambition can power the next global clean energy push

forces.title: Increased MNRE Budget Allocation Boosts Renewable Energy Push
forces.description: IBEF reports a significant increase in the Union Budget 2026-27 allocation for the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), reaching Rs. 44,614.67 crore (US$5.05 billion), a 40.52% rise over the previous year. This substantial budgetary push, driven by higher outlays for flagship schemes like PM Surya Ghar and enhanced support for solar deployment, energy storage, and domestic manufacturing, acts as a strong tailwind. It reinforces India’s commitment to large-scale renewable capacity expansion and the overarching energy transition.
forces.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

forces.title: India Achieves 20% Ethanol Blending Target Ahead of Schedule
forces.description: IBEF highlights India's successful achievement of its 20% ethanol blending with petrol target five years ahead of the 2030 deadline. This significant milestone underscores the country's commitment to green energy transition and provides a strong tailwind for the bioenergy and alternative fuels sector. It demonstrates the effectiveness of government programs like the Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) and creates a robust framework for further expansion and investment in sustainable biofuels, accelerating the decarbonization of the transport sector.
forces.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

forces.title: PM Surya Ghar Yojana Drives Rapid Rooftop Solar Adoption
forces.description: IBEF reports that the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has significantly accelerated rooftop solar adoption, crossing 40 lakh beneficiary households and leading to over 33 lakh rooftop solar systems with a cumulative capacity exceeding 12 GW installed by May 2026. With a target of 75 lakh rooftop solar installations by December 2026, this scheme acts as a powerful tailwind for the solar energy sector. It reinforces India's transition towards distributed renewable energy and energy self-reliance, driving substantial demand and investment.
forces.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

forces.title: National Green Hydrogen Mission and PLI Scheme Foster Domestic Manufacturing
forces.description: IBEF highlights two key policy initiatives: the National Green Hydrogen Mission (with an initial outlay of Rs. 19,744 crore) and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for High Efficiency Solar PV Modules (Tranche-II budget Rs. 19,500 crore). These programs serve as strong tailwinds, aiming to achieve 5 MMT of green hydrogen production by 2030 and establish 39,600 MW of domestic solar PV module manufacturing capacity. Both initiatives are critical for boosting self-reliance, driving gigawatt-scale manufacturing, and accelerating India's clean energy goals across strategic segments.
forces.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

forces.title: India's Power Sector Transformation Targets High Per Capita Electricity Consumption
forces.description: The Draft National Electricity Policy (NEP) 2026 aims to transform India’s power sector in line with Viksit Bharat @2047, targeting an increase in per capita electricity consumption to 2,000 kWh by 2030 and over 4,000 kWh by 2047. This ambitious target, coupled with an emphasis on large-scale renewable energy integration, deployment of energy storage systems, and grid modernization, acts as a significant upside driver. It creates immense long-term demand for clean power generation and associated infrastructure, ensuring reliable and affordable supply.
forces.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Global power conversion market tied to energy transition offers $95 billion opportunity by 2030.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects the global power conversion technology market to reach $95 billion by 2030, growing at a 7% CAGR from 2024. These technologies, including inverters, rectifiers, and DC-DC converters, are critical for integrating renewable energy into the grid and enabling efficient energy storage. While growth in supply-side renewable applications like solar PV is slowing, the overall market presents significant opportunities due to decarbonization and electrification trends, making efficient power conversion essential for a reliable energy future.
viewpoints.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

viewpoints.title: Growth in supply-side renewable power conversion slowing, contrasting with demand-side electrification.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey notes a deceleration in growth for power conversion technologies in supply-side renewable energy applications, with solar PV CAGR expected to decline by 2% from 2024-2030. This contrasts sharply with robust growth of 10% or more in demand-side applications like data centers and EVs, which are driving the overall power conversion market. This shift suggests a maturing renewable generation market and increasing demand for solutions integrating clean energy into diverse consumption points.
viewpoints.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

viewpoints.title: Diverging opportunities in power conversion, favoring complex, integrated solutions for growth.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey argues that while the overall power conversion market grows, opportunities diverge significantly by segment complexity. High-complexity areas like data centers, HVDC, and BESS offer compelling growth for players providing integrated, software-driven solutions (e.g., grid-forming control). In contrast, solar PV and heat pumps are commoditizing, demanding cost optimization. Investors are advised to target players with defensible depth in high-growth verticals and recurring revenue streams beyond hardware, given the application-specific nature of the market.
viewpoints.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

viewpoints.title: Hybrid AC/DC architecture is inevitable as DC-native sources and loads scale.
viewpoints.description: BCG argues that the energy system is undergoing a fundamental shift towards a hybrid AC/DC architecture. This is driven by the native DC nature of new energy sources like solar PV and storage like batteries, alongside increasing DC loads from data centers and EVs. The current AC-dominant grid infrastructure creates inefficiencies through multiple conversions. The report asserts that DC will complement AC by powering high-density, behind-the-meter applications, improving efficiency, and maximizing scarce grid connections, thus becoming a required architecture for future energy systems.
viewpoints.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

viewpoints.title: India's BESS market enters crucial execution phase, demanding bankable projects.
viewpoints.description: EY-Parthenon asserts that India's Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) market is transitioning from policy-led procurement to a critical "bankable execution" phase post-2026. While demand and tendered capacity are rapidly expanding (optimistic FTM deployment to ~255 GWh by 2032), only a tiny fraction of ~111 GWh tendered has translated into operational assets. Project viability now hinges on sound system architecture, financing closure, and managing lifecycle costs, underscoring that execution, not just demand, will dictate actual deployment.
viewpoints.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

viewpoints.title: India's nuclear energy re-emerges as a strategic pillar for low-carbon, baseload power.
viewpoints.description: EY-Parthenon declares India's nuclear energy sector is re-emerging as a strategic pillar to meet the country's rising energy demand, ensuring security, affordability, and decarbonization. With a target of 100 GW by 2047 and recent policy reforms like the SHANTI Act opening the market to private and foreign participation, nuclear is shifting from a marginal to a core contributor. The introduction of Bharat Small Reactors (BSRs) and significant budgetary commitments aim to build a multi-technology, future-ready nuclear ecosystem, offering firm, low-carbon baseload power to complement renewables.
viewpoints.source_title: How India’s nuclear ambition can power the next global clean energy push

viewpoints.title: India's ambitious renewable energy targets and policy support will drive unprecedented growth.
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights India's immense growth potential in renewable energy, backed by ambitious targets of 500 GW by 2030 and net-zero by 2070. Strong policy support, including increased MNRE allocation (Rs. 44,614.67 crore), PM Surya Ghar, SHP Development Scheme, and PLI for solar manufacturing, is fueling this expansion. With 20% ethanol blending already achieved and substantial FDI inflows (US$3.02 billion in FY26), India is positioned for unprecedented growth, attracting significant investment and reinforcing its commitment to a large-scale energy transition.

viewpoints.title: India's nuclear power capacity set for significant expansion by 2031-32.
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports that India is actively enhancing its nuclear power capacity, with government initiatives aiming to increase capacity from 8,780 MW in 2026-27 to 22,480 MW by 2031-32. This expansion is driven by the need to meet growing energy demands and achieve environmental goals, positioning nuclear as a key component in India's balancing act between energy availability, affordability, and sustainability. The move reflects a commitment to diversifying its energy mix beyond renewables.

demand_drivers.description: Commitment to 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030 and net-zero carbon emissions by 2070 drives capacity expansion.

demand_drivers.driver: Government initiatives and policy support
demand_drivers.description: Flagship schemes like PM Surya Ghar and enhanced support for solar deployment, energy storage, and domestic manufacturing.

market_sizing.methodology: Total installed capacity of renewable energy sources (Small Hydro Power, Wind Power, Solar Power, and Bio-Power) in India as of May 2026, excluding large hydro. This reflects significant progress towards the 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Strong additions in solar segment
demand_drivers.description: Continuous expansion of solar energy capacity contributes to increased generation output.

demand_drivers.driver: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
demand_drivers.description: Government scheme targeting rooftop solar installations in one crore households by 2026-27 drives significant adoption.

demand_drivers.driver: Government's ambitious renewable energy targets
demand_drivers.description: Overall targets for non-fossil fuel capacity push solar development and generation.

new_opportunities.description: The PM Surya Ghar scheme is accelerating installations and promoting energy independence at the household level.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Distributed renewable energy and energy self-reliance through rooftop solar

market_sizing.methodology: India's solar power generation for FY26, which has surpassed Japan's 96,459 GWh, making India the world's third-largest solar energy producer. This demonstrates strong output and contributes to India's overall renewable energy goals.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Ambitious target of 100 GW production by 2030
demand_drivers.description: Government goals are driving significant investment and deployment in the wind energy sector.

demand_drivers.driver: Strong additions in wind segments
demand_drivers.description: Continuous growth in installed wind power capacity contributes to India's renewable energy mix.

pnl_drivers.description: Over 18 GW for wind turbines and components supports the build-out of new projects and reduces import reliance.

market_sizing.methodology: India's current installed wind energy capacity, which is making significant strides towards the ambitious target of 100 GW by 2030. India ranks fourth worldwide in terms of total installed wind power capacity.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Government's proactive stance towards accelerated hydropower development
demand_drivers.description: Policy support and initiatives are driving new project construction and capacity expansion.

demand_drivers.driver: Prediction of higher rainfall by IMD
demand_drivers.description: Favorable meteorological conditions enhance the potential for hydropower generation.

new_opportunities.description: An outlay of Rs. 2,584.60 crore (US$ 0.29 billion) for 2026-31 to support installation of ~1,500 MW capacity, catalyzing investments of around Rs. 15,000.00 crore (US$ 1.70 billion) in decentralized renewable energy.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme

market_sizing.methodology: India’s total hydropower potential and the portion currently utilized (over ~50 GW). India has been identified as the nation with the fifth-largest hydropower production capacity in the world by the International Hydropower Association (IHA). An additional 15 GW of projects are under construction, which will increase the country's total hydro capacity from 42 GW to 67 GW by 2031-32.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Growing energy demands
demand_drivers.description: India's rapidly expanding economy requires a significant increase in power generation capacity.

demand_drivers.driver: Achieving environmental goals
demand_drivers.description: Nuclear power provides dependable, round-the-clock, low-carbon electricity, supporting decarbonization targets.

market_sizing.methodology: Government target to increase nuclear power capacity from the current 8,780 MW in 2026-27 to 22,480 MW by 2031-32, to meet growing energy demands and achieve environmental goals.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: India's 20% ethanol blending target
demand_drivers.description: The target was achieved five years ahead of its 2030 deadline, creating sustained demand for bioethanol.

demand_drivers.driver: Decarbonization efforts and need for alternative fuels
demand_drivers.description: Bioethanol contributes to reducing carbon emissions in the transport sector.

new_opportunities.description: The scheme supports commercial-scale production, expanding the bioenergy sector.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Advanced bioethanol projects using renewable feedstocks

market_sizing.methodology: Financial support approved under the amended Pradhan Mantri Jaiv Indhan - Vatavaran Anukool Fasal Awashesh Nivaran (PM JI-VAN) Yojana for 2G bioethanol projects, including commercial-scale initiatives like those in Panipat, Haryana. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance for advanced bioethanol projects using renewable feedstocks.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Government commitments to net-zero emissions and renewable energy targets
demand_drivers.description: India's targets of 500 GW renewable energy by 2030 and net-zero by 2070 provide a strong policy framework for investors.

demand_drivers.driver: Favorable policies and incentives
demand_drivers.description: Government support schemes and initiatives attract foreign capital into the clean energy sector.

market_sizing.methodology: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) equity inflows attracted by India's non-conventional energy sector in FY26, representing approximately 5.1% of the total FDI received during the fiscal year. This reaffirms the sector's continued attractiveness to global investors.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Regional energy security and clean energy goals
demand_drivers.description: Large-scale RE and BESS projects address energy needs in remote regions and contribute to decarbonization.

demand_drivers.driver: Integration of RE with storage
demand_drivers.description: The project combines renewable generation with storage to ensure reliable power supply.

new_opportunities.description: Such projects address critical infrastructure gaps and leverage renewable resources in challenging geographies.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Large-scale RE and BESS projects in remote regions

market_sizing.methodology: Proposed renewable energy (RE) capacity and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity by MNRE in Ladakh. The Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Detailed Project Report (DPR) have been completed as of 2026, indicating project readiness.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Government's commitment to expanding renewable energy infrastructure
demand_drivers.description: The Solar Park Scheme aims to facilitate large-scale solar project development and meet renewable energy targets.

new_opportunities.description: The scheme creates dedicated zones for solar projects, simplifying land acquisition and grid connectivity.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Large-scale solar project development within designated parks

market_sizing.methodology: Cumulative sanctioned capacity of 55 solar parks across 13 states under the Solar Park Scheme as of October 31, 2025. Of this, 14,922 MW of solar capacity has already been commissioned, with the remaining capacity under various stages of implementation. The scheme timeline has been extended until March 31, 2029, with new approvals limited to those granted up to March 31, 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Government's commitment to clean energy transition
demand_drivers.description: The mission aims to position India as a global hub for green hydrogen production and export.

demand_drivers.driver: Target of 5 MMT green hydrogen production by 2030
demand_drivers.description: This ambitious production target drives investment in infrastructure, technology, and manufacturing.

new_opportunities.description: Funding supports the development of green hydrogen production facilities and demonstration projects.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Green hydrogen production and pilot projects

new_opportunities.description: Investment in research to advance electrolyser efficiency, storage, and transport solutions.
new_opportunities.opportunity: R&D in green hydrogen technologies

market_sizing.methodology: Total initial outlay approved by the Union Cabinet for the National Green Hydrogen Mission. This includes specific allocations for the Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) programme (Rs. 17,490 crore), pilot projects (Rs. 1,466 crore), R&D (Rs. 400 crore), and other Mission components (Rs. 388 crore).
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative
demand_drivers.description: Government's push for self-reliance in critical sectors, including solar PV manufacturing.

demand_drivers.driver: Need for domestic manufacturing capacity for solar PV modules
demand_drivers.description: Reducing import dependence and creating local jobs in the solar energy sector.

new_opportunities.description: The PLI scheme incentivizes large-scale production of high-efficiency solar modules within India.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Gigawatt-scale domestic solar PV module manufacturing

market_sizing.methodology: Budget allocation under Tranche-II of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for the National Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules. Letters of Award were issued in April 2023 for establishing 39,600 MW of fully or partially integrated solar PV module manufacturing units, aiming for gigawatt-scale domestic capacity.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Need for grid stability and integration of intermittent renewable energy sources
demand_drivers.description: Pumped hydro storage provides essential grid balancing services for fluctuating solar and wind power.

demand_drivers.driver: Demand for flexible energy storage
demand_drivers.description: Large-scale storage solutions are critical for managing peak demand and ensuring round-the-clock power supply.

new_opportunities.description: These projects offer significant opportunities for investment and infrastructure development in the energy storage sector.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Large-scale pumped hydro storage projects

market_sizing.methodology: Investment and capacity of two pumped storage projects being developed by Avaada Group in Maharashtra (2,400 MW Pawana Falyan and 1,200 MW Sirsala). This highlights significant private investment in large-scale energy storage infrastructure.
market_sizing.source_title: Renewable Energy Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: India’s commitment to large-scale renewable capacity expansion
demand_drivers.description: The increased budget supports ambitious targets for renewable energy deployment and energy transition.

demand_drivers.driver: Enhanced support for solar deployment, energy storage, and domestic manufacturing
demand_drivers.description: Specific allocations for key segments drive growth and localization within the renewable energy sector.

market_sizing.methodology: Union Budget 2026-27 allocation for the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), reflecting a 40.52% increase over the 2025-26 Budget Estimates of Rs. 31,749.38 crore (US$3.75 billion). This increase is driven by higher outlays towards flagship schemes and enhanced support for solar deployment, energy storage, and domestic manufacturing.
